notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware was attached or run. The upstream SAPIEN environment needs a GPU and the PartNet Mobility assets and was not importable where the gate runs, so fake.py is the package's pure Python analytic stand-in and was not compared with it; the sim backend (gym.make('OpenCabinetDoor-v0')) was not run. The fake returns the state-mode vector shape of the clone (75 values: 13 cabinet pose/velocity + 2*8 padded internal values + 8 target indicators + a 38-value agent state) but only the cabinet root quaternion, the target joint qpos and the target indicator carry modelled values; the rest are placeholder zeros, and the observation gaps say so. The fake uses the legacy four-value step return, so a time-limit end is reported as terminated rather than truncated. Five warnings are expected and left unfixed: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge only stores the seed for the next reset, so it makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the integer inputs and the action-space values the bridge derives (ticks, seed twice, action.values). Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. The e-stop is the runtime's software latch on a simulated R0 device: no independent hardware stop exists or is claimed. gate.digest is the digest line the check printed (the report file's own digest excludes its clock).
